page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ds_v4 is an x86_64 architecture virtual server belonging to the EDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores running at 2.6 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The system is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 307 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between memory capacity and processing speed. The server exhibits weak performance, falling into the bottom 25% for both single-core and multi-core CPU tests, including stress-ng, Passmark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is also weak, though Passmark memory scores and single-threaded gzip compression perform at an average level in the middle 50%. Database operations, such as Redis SET and Passmark database tests, fall into the bottom 25%, reflecting CPU-bound limitations despite the large RAM allocation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers high memory density relative to its vCPU count, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU throughput. It is best suited for workloads such as medium-sized databases, caching layers, and memory-intensive text processing tasks that benefit from 64 GB of RAM and local SSD storage but can tolerate lower CPU performance.
